subject: government

items.question: Which power did the national government LACK under the Articles of Confederation, causing serious problems?
items.question_es: ¿Qué poder le FALTABA al gobierno nacional bajo los Artículos de la Confederación?

options.A: The power to tax the states and citizens directly
options.C: The power to run a post office

distractor_rationale.A: Correct — Congress could only request money from states, leaving it unable to pay debts.
distractor_rationale.B: Congress could declare war under the Articles.

items.answer_explanation: No taxing power left the national government too weak to pay debts or respond to crises like Shays's Rebellion.

remediation.next_step: Re-anchor on the primary source, re-teach the 3 vocabulary terms (EN/ES), then re-attempt a parallel item.

misconception_by_option.B: Congress could declare war under the Articles.

items.question: Shays's Rebellion (1786–1787) is significant because it:
items.question_es: La Rebelión de Shays (1786–1787) es importante porque:

options.A: proved the Articles created a strong military
options.B: exposed the national government's weakness and pushed leaders toward a new constitution
options.D: was led by King George III

distractor_rationale.A: The opposite — the government could not raise forces to stop it.
distractor_rationale.B: Correct — its failure to respond convinced leaders to replace the Articles.
distractor_rationale.C: The war had already ended in 1783.
distractor_rationale.D: It was a farmers' uprising in Massachusetts, unrelated to the king.

items.answer_explanation: The rebellion revealed the Articles' fatal weakness and helped trigger the 1787 Convention.

items.question: The Anti-Federalists agreed to support the Constitution mainly on the condition that:
items.question_es: Los antifederalistas apoyaron la Constitución principalmente con la condición de que:

options.D: a bill of rights be added to protect individual liberties

distractor_rationale.A: They accepted a new constitution, not the old Articles.
distractor_rationale.B: They feared concentrated power; a life term is the opposite of their aim.
distractor_rationale.C: They wanted to PROTECT state power.
distractor_rationale.D: Correct — their central demand was a bill of rights against a too-powerful central government.

items.answer_explanation: The promise of a Bill of Rights secured ratification.

remediation.next_step: Re-anchor on the primary source, re-teach the 3 vocabulary terms (EN/ES), then re-attempt a parallel item.

items.question: The Preamble begins 'We the People.' Which principle does this phrase express?
items.question_es: El Preámbulo comienza 'Nosotros el Pueblo'. ¿Qué principio expresa esta frase?

options.A: Popular sovereignty — government power comes from the people

distractor_rationale.A: Correct — authority flows from the people themselves.
distractor_rationale.B: Judicial review comes from Article III / Marbury, not the Preamble's opening.
distractor_rationale.C: Separation of powers is a structural principle, not the meaning of 'We the People.'

items.answer_explanation: 'We the People' declares popular sovereignty — the source of the Constitution's authority.

remediation.next_step: Re-anchor on the primary source, re-teach the 3 vocabulary terms (EN/ES), then re-attempt a parallel item.

misconception_by_option.B: Judicial review comes from Article III / Marbury, not the Preamble's opening.

items.question: The power of courts to declare a law unconstitutional is called:
items.question_es: El poder de los tribunales para declarar inconstitucional una ley se llama:

distractor_rationale.A: The veto is an executive power over legislation.
distractor_rationale.B: Impeachment removes officials; it does not void laws.
distractor_rationale.C: Correct — judicial review, established in Marbury v. Madison (1803).
distractor_rationale.D: Popular sovereignty is the source of authority, not a court power.

items.answer_explanation: Judicial review lets courts void unconstitutional acts — a key check.

items.question: To ratify a constitutional amendment under Article V requires approval by:
items.question_es: Ratificar una enmienda constitucional bajo el Artículo V requiere la aprobación de:

distractor_rationale.A: The president has no formal role in amending the Constitution.
distractor_rationale.B: A simple national majority is not the standard.
distractor_rationale.C: Courts interpret, they do not ratify amendments.
distractor_rationale.D: Correct — three-fourths of the states must ratify.

items.answer_explanation: Article V requires a 2/3 proposal and 3/4 state ratification — a high, federalism-protecting bar.

items.question: In Federalist No. 10, Madison argues a large republic is better than a pure democracy because it:
items.question_es: En El Federalista No. 10, Madison sostiene que una república grande es mejor que una democracia pura porque:

options.B: gives all power to one leader
options.D: better controls the dangers of faction

distractor_rationale.A: Madison expects factions to persist; the aim is to control, not eliminate them.
distractor_rationale.B: Concentrating power is the opposite of Madison's design.
distractor_rationale.D: Correct — a large republic dilutes and checks factions.

items.answer_explanation: Madison's large-republic argument is that scale and representation control faction.
